title_en: A mysterious gap hints at black holes born from stars that never exploded
title_zh: 一个神秘的缺口暗示了从未爆炸过的恒星产生的黑洞

paragraphs.en: The biggest stars in the universe often end their lives in spectacular explosions called supernovae, hurling enormous amounts of material into space. Their remaining cores collapse under gravity, forming neutron stars or, in some cases, black holes. But scientists have long suspected that some massive stars meet a very different fate. Instead of exploding, they may collapse directly into neutron stars or black holes, effectively disappearing without a bang.
paragraphs.zh: 宇宙中最大的恒星往往以被称为超新星的壮观光爆结束一生，将巨量物质抛射到太空中。它们残留的核心在引力作用下坍缩，形成中子星，某些情况下则形成黑洞。但科学家长期以来一直怀疑，一些大质量恒星有着截然不同的归宿。它们可能不发生爆炸，而是直接坍缩成中子星或黑洞，实际上悄无声息地消失了。

paragraphs.en: New research led by Caltech has uncovered intriguing evidence that this quieter form of stellar death may help explain the origins of many black holes. Using gravitational wave observations from the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA detector network, researchers identified patterns suggesting that a distinct population of black holes could have formed from stars that never went supernova. Although the findings do not directly confirm the existence of these failed supernovae, they closely match theoretical predictions about how such black holes should be distributed.
paragraphs.zh: 由加州理工学院（Caltech）牵头的一项新研究发现了耐人寻味的证据，表明这种更为安静的恒星死亡方式可能有助于解释许多黑洞的起源。研究人员利用LIGO、Virgo和KAGRA探测器网络的引力波观测数据，识别出一些模式，暗示可能存在一个独特的黑洞群体，它们由从未发生超新星的恒星形成。尽管这些发现并未直接证实这类“失败超新星”的存在，但它们与关于此类黑洞应如何分布的理论预测高度吻合。

paragraphs.en: The discoveries build on a decade of gravitational wave astronomy. LIGO, the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory, is funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF) and operates detectors in Louisiana and Washington. In 2015, the observatory made history by directly detecting gravitational waves for the first time. These tiny disturbances in spacetime were generated by two black holes colliding. Since then, LIGO has teamed up with the Virgo observatory in Italy and the Kamioka Gravitational-wave Detector (KAGRA) in Japan. Together, the network has recorded more than 300 black hole collisions.
paragraphs.zh: 这些发现建立在十年来引力波天文学的基础之上。LIGO即激光干涉引力波天文台（Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory），由美国国家科学基金会（NSF）资助，在路易斯安那州和华盛顿州运行探测器。2015年，该天文台首次直接探测到引力波，创造了历史。这些时空中的微小扰动由两个黑洞碰撞产生。此后，LIGO与意大利的Virgo天文台以及日本的Kamioka引力波探测器（KAGRA）展开合作。该网络迄今已记录到300多次黑洞碰撞。

paragraphs.en: "A vast majority of the merging black holes in the universe are about 10 times the mass of our Sun," says LIGO team member Katerina Chatziioannou, a Caltech physics professor and William H. Hurt Scholar. "Our data are showing that this group of black holes may have a common origin -- they may be a distinct subpopulation that failed to go supernova. These results represent a connection between the gravitational-wave data and underlying astrophysics we are trying to extract."
paragraphs.zh: “宇宙中绝大多数并合黑洞的质量约为太阳的10倍，”LIGO团队成员、加州理工学院物理学教授、William H. Hurt学者卡捷琳娜·哈齐约安努（Katerina Chatziioannou）说。“我们的数据表明，这一黑洞群体可能有共同的起源——它们可能是一个未能发生超新星的独特亚群。这些结果代表了引力波数据与我们试图提取的底层天体物理学之间的联系。”

paragraphs.en: Chatziioannou led the study, which was published in Physical Review D . The lead author, Isaac Legred (PhD '25), is now a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and completed the work while at Caltech. Jacob Golomb (PhD '25), a former member of Chatziioannou's research group who now works at Asari AI, also contributed to the research.
paragraphs.zh: 哈齐约安努领导了这项研究，论文发表在《物理评论D》（Physical Review D）上。第一作者艾萨克·莱格瑞德（Isaac Legred，2025年博士毕业）现为伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校的博士后研究员，此项工作是在加州理工学院期间完成的。哈齐约安努研究组前成员、现就职于Asari AI的雅各布·戈隆布（Jacob Golomb，2025年博士毕业）也参与了这项研究。

paragraphs.en: Despite decades of investigation, astronomers have yet to confirm a specific case of a failed supernova. The theory, however, has a strong scientific foundation. Researchers have proposed that many merging black holes weighing approximately 10 times as much as the Sun may have originated from stars that collapsed without exploding. In these mergers, either the heavier black hole or both black holes could have formed through this process. The Caltech team set out to determine whether existing gravitational wave observations supported that possibility.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管经过数十年的研究，天文学家尚未确认任何一例具体的失败超新星。然而，这一理论有着坚实的科学基础。研究人员提出，许多质量约为太阳10倍的并合黑洞可能起源于未发生爆炸便坍缩的恒星。在这些并合事件中，较重的黑洞或两个黑洞都可能通过这一过程形成。加州理工学院团队着手确定现有引力波观测是否支持这一可能性。

paragraphs.en: To investigate, the scientists examined the masses of black holes involved in 257 mergers detected by the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA network during the past decade. A striking pattern emerged. Black holes weighing roughly 10 times the mass of the Sun were exceptionally common, appearing in about three-quarters of the merger sample.
paragraphs.zh: 为了探究这一问题，科学家检查了过去十年间LIGO、Virgo和KAGRA网络探测到的257次并合事件中所涉黑洞的质量。一个引人注目的模式浮现出来。质量约为太阳10倍的黑洞异常常见，出现在约四分之三的并合样本中。
